The '''Soruus system''' was a part of the [[Cronese Mandate/Legends|Cronese Mandate]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]]. It contained the [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Soruus]], which was an active [[Merchant/Legends|trade]] world under the [[Kingdom of Cron]], and remained associated with [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] contests dating back to that [[Time/Legends|time]] [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]] later. The system's [[Soruus system's provincial government|provincial government]] sentenced criminals to fight to [[Death/Legends|death]] in arenas, and the [[Min-Dal Company|Min-Dal]] corporation developed and tested the prototype [[JX4 Gladiator Prototype|JX4]] personal [[battle armor]] suits there.

==Description==
The Soruus system was located in the [[Cronese Mandate/Legends|Cronese Mandate]] [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of the [[Tion Cluster/Legends|Tion Cluster]],<ref name="Xim" /> situated within [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] portion of<ref name="The Slice" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA" /> It lay on the [[Greater Cronese Arc]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperspace route]], which linked it to the [[Barancar system/Legends|Barancar]] and [[Pasmin system/Legends|Pasmin systems]]. The Soruus [[Star system/Legends|system]] contained<ref name="Xim" /> the terrestrial<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-part-3-xim-the-despot|series=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|text=Part 3 - "Xim the Despot"}}</ref> [[Planet/Legends|world]] of the [[Soruus|same name]].<ref name="Xim" />

==History==
[[File:Gladiator_armor.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The prototype JX4 gladiator armor was developed and tested in arenas in the Soruus system.]]
Between around [[25,150 BBY]] and [[25,130 BBY]], the Soruus system was a member of the [[Kingdom of Cron]]. During the reign of [[Cronese]] [[King of Cron|King]] [[Xim/Legends|Xim]], Soruus was an active [[Merchant/Legends|trade]] world and was also famous for [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] spectacles, with tradition associated with them surviving the decline of most other local commerce over the subsequent [[Millennium/Legends|millennia]].<ref name="Xim" /> At one point, a statue of Xim manufactured on<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="TEA" /> world [[Centares/Legends|Centares]] was erected on Soruus.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The merchant, [[Philosopher/Legends|philosopher]], and [[Historian/Legends|historian]]<ref name="Xim" /> [[Bleys Harand]] eventually traveled to the worlds of the Tion Cluster, including Soruus, in search of a contemporary visual depiction of Xim.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The [[Soruus system's provincial government]] sentenced criminals to fight to the [[Death/Legends|death]] in large arenas<ref name="Gundark">''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]''</ref> in the system<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|185|JX4}}</ref> for public entertainment, a practice that continued for many [[Standard year/Legends|years]]. The [[Min-Dal Company|Min-Dal]] corporation<ref name="Gundark" /> developed<ref name="CSWE" /> and tested prototypes of the [[JX4 Gladiator Prototype|JX4]] personal [[battle armor]] suit in those gladiatorial contests. At some point<ref name="Gundark" /> by [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="Date">''[[Gundark's Fantastic Technology: Personal Gear]]'' establishes that the escape of the [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiators]] from the Soruus [[Star system/Legends|system]] arenas took place by the [[Great ReSynchronization calendar|date]] "44:2:3:49," which corresponds to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> however, a group of gladiators wearing the armor suits escaped from the arenas, going on to commit atrocious crimes.<ref name="Gundark" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Soruus system was first mentioned in "[[Outlaw Battle Armor]]," a [[West End Games]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' source article written by [[Philip Tobin]] and published in the [[August]] [[1994]] [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 3|third issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]'' magazine.<ref name="Journal3">{{JournalCite|3|Outlaw Battle Armor}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed it in grid square S-6.<ref name="TEA" />
